stem: A Massachusetts collaborative practice agreement was properly written, signed and within the supervising physician's scope when it was made twenty-six months ago. Neither party has reviewed it since. The pharmacist proposes to keep co-managing referred patients while a review is scheduled. What is the position?

choices.text: The agreement stands, because nothing in it has changed since it was signed.
The agreement stands, provided the pharmacist documents that a review is pending.
The agreement stands until the supervising physician gives notice of termination.
The agreement is out of currency, because review and renewal fall due biennially.
The agreement is void, and every act taken under it in month 25 must be reported.

explanation.core_reasoning: The M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2(a) definition provides that each collaborative practice agreement SHALL BE SUBJECT TO REVIEW AND RENEWAL ON A BIENNIAL BASIS. Valid constitution at the outset does not keep an agreement current; the biennial review is a continuing condition, and twenty-six months without one leaves the agreement outside it.

choice_analysis.A: Currency is a separate requirement from constitution.
choice_analysis.B: A pending review is not a review.
choice_analysis.C: Termination by the physician is a different event from lapse of currency.
choice_analysis.D: Correct: the biennial review and renewal condition has not been met.
choice_analysis.E: The statute imposes no reporting duty of that kind here.

related_facts: The agreement must also include individually developed prescriptive guidelines
explanation.mpje_trap: Candidates check the formation requirements, find them satisfied, and never ask whether the instrument is still current.

reasoning_steps: Confirm the agreement was validly constituted
Apply the separate biennial review and renewal condition
Measure the elapsed period against it
